players.product: Neon final-inspection systems for HBM stacks and advanced packages, plus thermal test handlers

quarterly_data.signal: HBM INSPECTION OUTLOOK RAISED: CEO says Cohu continues to see strong momentum for final inspection of HBM3 and HBM4 and is investing to keep pace with design requirements for next-generation HBM5. Cohu now forecasts Neon HBM platform revenue growing 80% year-over-year to approximately $20 million in 2026 (CFO: the prior $15 million-$20 million HBM range is now at the higher end). In Q1 Cohu secured a significant volume repeat order for Neon inspection from a U.S.-headquartered customer and from a Korean customer (neither named). Inspection and metrology orders were up 64% year-over-year and the inspection business is estimated at approximately $70 million of revenue this year. HBM inspection is counted as about $100 million of the ~$750 million computing opportunity pipeline.
quarterly_data.figure: Neon HBM revenue growing 80% to approximately $20 million (2026); inspection revenue approximately $70 million; inspection orders up 64% YoY; HBM inspection pipeline $100 million

players.product: Eclipse thermal test handlers for AI processors, Neon inspection, flexible ATE and PACE analytics software

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 RESULTS: revenue $125.1 million, above the guidance midpoint; recurring revenue (mainly consumables) was 60% of total; no customer above 10% of sales; non-GAAP gross margin 46.5% on a favorable recurring mix (roughly 50% on recurring vs roughly 40% on systems). Orders rose 57% year-over-year, with the computing segment up about 211% year-over-year; test handler orders up 54% and semiconductor test orders up 163%. Estimated semiconductor test utilization rose to 78% (industrial 79%).
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue $125.1 million; orders up 57% YoY; computing orders up about 211%; gross margin 46.5%; test utilization 78%

quarterly_data.signal: GUIDANCE: Q2 2026 revenue expected to rise 15% sequentially and 34% year-over-year to approximately $144 million, ±$7 million, driven by the high-performance compute ramp and automotive/industrial recovery (HPC systems revenue up about $10 million quarter-over-quarter, just under half of the Q2 increase; about half driven by non-compute markets, fundamentally industrial). Full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook raised to 20%-25%; Q3 expected similar to Q2 in the $144 million-$145 million range, Q4 possibly down mid single digit on seasonality. Q2 gross margin approximately 44% and full-year in the mid-40% range because of higher initial costs to ramp the new Eclipse supply chain and production, plus about 10 basis points each from energy/freight and higher cost of memory ICs. OpEx about $53 million in Q2, low $50 million range through the second half.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue approximately $144 million, ±$7 million; FY2026 growth 20%-25%; Q2 gross margin approximately 44%

quarterly_data.signal: COMPUTING PIPELINE AND HPC OUTLOOK RAISED: CEO sees a computing segment opportunity pipeline (a SAM tallied from a targeted list of customers, not a TAM) of approximately $750 million — roughly $650 million in test handlers plus $100 million from HBM inspection — across 12 customers (five in qualification, seven in early engagement). FY2026 high-performance computing revenue outlook raised from $60 million-$85 million to approximately $80 million-$100 million, mostly from the Eclipse handler after a successful Eclipse qualification at one account; HPC systems revenue in the first half of 2026 roughly about $30 million. The five qualifying customers (all Eclipse thermal, a $10 million-$40 million annual spread depending on the customer) represent an incremental $200 million opportunity starting late this year, largely 2027; some qualifications expected to be completed by early Q3; the remaining $450 million-$500 million in engagement should move into qualification later this year or early 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: pipeline approximately $750 million (roughly $650 million test handlers + $100 million HBM inspection); FY2026 HPC revenue approximately $80 million-$100 million; $200 million in qualification

quarterly_data.signal: TWO MAJOR ECLIPSE WINS: (1) a U.S. fabless customer (not named) developing server and inference devices standardized on Eclipse with T-Core active thermal control across multiple device generations and is adopting PAICe Prescriptive analytics software — an estimated $100 million incremental revenue opportunity at this account over the next three years; (2) another U.S.-based fabless customer (not named) ordered Eclipse for data center computing, mobile and automotive processors, used by the customer and its OSATs. A $20 million system order came with $330,000 a year of software subscription (approximately $5 million lifetime recurring revenue); software ARR is about $1.2 million, attach rate about 1.3% of systems, software revenue expected close to $3 million this year.
quarterly_data.figure: estimated $100 million incremental revenue opportunity over the next three years at one U.S. fabless account; $20 million system order with $330,000 a year software

quarterly_data.signal: DEMAND BROADENING BEYOND GPUs: CEO says that since a little more than a quarter ago demand has pivoted toward large CPU, ASIC accelerators and network processors, spreading out from what had been largely a singular customer driving GPU capacity, as inference picks up. Accelerators and HPC processors need precise temperature-controlled test, which is where Cohu's thermal handlers are valued.

CAPACITY / SUPPLY CHOKE POINTS: thermal handlers are running at a 14 week cycle time, but lead time depends on backlog (CEO: a $30 million order would not all ship in 14 weeks; it is spread over several months). Cohu is meeting suppliers to identify choke points, particularly for its thermal heads, hiring in Malaysia and re-laying out the Malaysia facility for more floor space, and expanding production capacity into 2027. Order shipments ramp in Q3 with some falling into Q4. Capex targeted at about 2% of revenue in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 14 week cycle time on thermal handlers; capex about 2% of revenue in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: AI POWER AND SILICON PHOTONICS BEACHHEADS: the Diamondx tester was qualified for testing power devices as customers adopt GaN to serve AI data centers moving to 800 V DC infrastructure and rack-scale server boards such as the new Vera Rubin platform; high current contactors for AI power applications saw increased adoption. Cohu received a multi-unit order for a new silicon photonics solution — interface contactors (CEO: 'sort of 10,000 or so contactors that we sold several of') for silicon photonics switches at one of the large accounts (not named) — which the CEO calls a beachhead business not included in the $750 million pipeline; Cohu is working to pair its handler with the contactors.
